title: Accessory Physics Workshop
description: A physics-based accessory fitting simulation where the user manipulates gravitational forces, wind vectors, and spring constraints to guide a pair of sunglasses onto Michelle's face. The user must balance multiple coupled physical parameters while conserving total system energy, with full undo/redo support for each adjustment step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive physics accessory simulation. Load Michelle.glb as a standing character at the scene center and SunglassesKhronos.glb floating 2 units above and 1 unit in front of her head. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.6, 3.5) looking at Michelle's head height. Add a HemisphereLight (sky 0x87CEEB, ground 0x444444, intensity 1.0), a DirectionalLight with shadows from (3, 5, 3), and a subtle ambient light. Implement a simplified physics system where the sunglasses are affected by: (1) gravity vector adjustable via a 2D XY pad on-screen, (2) wind force adjustable via a horizontal slider, (3) a spring-damper attraction force toward a target point on Michelle's nose bridge adjustable via a stiffness slider, and (4) air resistance via a drag coefficient slider. Display a real-time energy bar showing kinetic + potential + spring energy, enforcing conservation: total energy stays constant unless the user injects or removes energy via a dedicated energy dial (fifth input). The sunglasses must rotate realistically based on net torque from all forces. Implement these required interactions: adjust gravity direction (steps 1-2), set wind force (step 3), tune spring stiffness (steps 4-5), adjust drag (step 6), inject energy via dial (steps 7-8), fine-tune gravity to guide descent (steps 9-10), and use undo/redo buttons (steps 11-12 to correct overshooting). Maintain a full action history stack supporting at least 20 undo/redo levels. Each parameter change is one discrete action pushed to the stack. When sunglasses reach within 0.05 units of the nose bridge target with velocity below 0.01, snap them onto Michelle's face with a green glow particle burst and display a success message. Show all parameter values in a semi-transparent HUD panel on the left side. Animate Michelle with a subtle idle breathing motion using sinusoidal vertex offset on her chest area. The ground should be a 10x10 grid plane with soft shadows.
